title: Research: odd-prime D_{2p} inverse-rotation four-call floor (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Answers open question 1 of [#1953](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1953) (`d10-reflection-sharing`): does the inverse-rotation pair keep its direct four-call tariff in `D_{2p}` for odd primes `p≥7`?

**Yes on the certified range** `p∈{5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31}`:

- Target `diag([st],[ts],[e])` in `M₃(F₂[D_{2p}])` with paid labels `{s,t}` and all 28 rank-one idempotents.
- Exhaustive length-≤3 search: **178809** candidates per prime (**1 609 281** total) → **0** exact endpoint hits.
- Direct word `D_{E₀₀}(s) D_{E₀₀}(t) D_{E₁₁}(t) D_{E₁₁}(s)` attains the target on every certified `p`, so the paid-call minimum is exactly **4**.
- At `p=5`, primary state digests match the pinned D10 certificate byte-for-byte.

This is a **finite certified-range** theorem, not a proof for every odd prime and not a physical supplier invoice. **No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/odd-prime-dihedral-inverse-rotation/`
- Tip: `d3bb257fee7c5dbdd4bd1ff25df9df799d76a7c2`
- Base: `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f` (CrocSwap/main; preferred pin `20ecf289…` had moved)
- Scope: **refined** — multi-prime inverse-rotation census answering #1953 OQ1 on the disclosed range

Closest prior: [#1953](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1953) (D10 / `p=5`); [#1881](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1881) (even `D₈`); [#1966](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1966) (odd-dihedral **reflection** tariffs — different endpoint). Soft overlap ≈0.35–0.55 vs D10 (shared encoding kernels; new 9-prime cert); ≈0.2–0.4 vs #1966.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/odd-prime-dihedral-inverse-rotation/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/odd-prime-dihedral-inverse-rotation/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/odd-prime-dihedral-inverse-rotation/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/odd-prime-dihedral-inverse-rotation/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/odd-prime-dihedral-inverse-rotation
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_ODD_PRIME_DIHEDRAL_INVERSE_ROTATION primes=[5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31] min_calls=4 words_le3_per_prime=178809 total_words=1609281 hits=0 p5_crosscheck=true no_new_kappa
PASS_INDEPENDENT_ODD_PRIME_DIHEDRAL_INVERSE_ROTATION primes=[5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31] min_calls=4 hits=0 no_new_kappa
PASS_ODD_PRIME_DIHEDRAL_INVERSE_ROTATION_PACKAGE_TESTS groups=4
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/odd-prime-dihedral-inverse-rotation outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`. Full verify is slow (minutes; ~1.6M words).

Credit [#1953](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1953) for the D10 inverse-rotation four-call minimum and OQ1; [#1881](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1881) for the even-order D8 floor; [#1966](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1966) for odd-dihedral reflection tariffs (distinct endpoint). Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions / limitations

1. Does a torsion-aware invariant prove the four-call floor for every odd prime without a separate census?
2. Does any odd prime `p>31` admit a three-call inverse-rotation share?
3. Is there a justified native supplier/compiler for a paid two-reflection alphabet realizing this endpoint?
